# Playbook: Making a Weak Text-Only LLM (groq/compound) Produce Excellent Animated Websites Through Scaffolding Alone

The thesis holds, and there's strong evidence for *why*: Anthropic's own engineering team documented that even a frontier model (Claude), *without* design scaffolding, "produces the same purple-gradient, Inter-on-white, three-card-with-rounded-corners design repeatedly," and that a single skill file flips it to look "like it was made by an actual designer." The quality delta on frontend is dominated by the prompt, not the model. A weak model + the right scaffolding therefore closes most of the gap on this narrow domain. Below are the concrete techniques, ranked by impact, each pastable into a system prompt or skill file.

---

## TIER 1 — Highest impact: kill "AI slop" by banning defaults and forcing aesthetic commitment

This is the single biggest lever. The exact mechanism Anthropic ships in its frontend-design skill is: (1) name the failure mode, (2) ban specific defaults by name, (3) supply loaded aesthetic vocabulary, (4) force a committed choice *before* any code. Paste this block near-verbatim — it is Anthropic's own distilled aesthetics prompt:

```
<frontend_aesthetics>
You tend to converge toward generic, "on distribution" outputs. In frontend
design, this creates what users call the "AI slop" aesthetic. Avoid this: make
creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight. Focus on:

Typography: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid
generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices.

Color & Theme: Commit to a cohesive aesthetic. Use CSS variables for consistency.
Dominant colors with sharp accents outperform timid, evenly-distributed palettes.
Draw from IDE themes and cultural aesthetics for inspiration.

Motion: Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Prioritize CSS-only
solutions. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with
staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered
micro-interactions.

Backgrounds: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors.
Layer CSS gradients, use geometric patterns, or add contextual effects.

Avoid generic AI-generated aesthetics:
- Overused font families (Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts, Space Grotesk)
- Clichéd color schemes (particularly purple gradients on white backgrounds)
- Predictable layouts and component patterns
- Cookie-cutter design that lacks context-specific character

Make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context.
</frontend_aesthetics>
```

Source: [Anthropic Claude Cookbook — Prompting for frontend aesthetics](https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/coding-prompting-for-frontend-aesthetics).

**Commitment-forcing step** (critical for a weak model — it can't be trusted to "feel" its way to a direction): make the model emit a one-line design manifesto *before* writing any code. Provide named directions so it picks an extreme rather than the median:

> Before writing code, output exactly one line: `DIRECTION: <one of: Linear-style minimal-dark | editorial/serif | brutalist | neo-brutalist | glassmorphism | art-deco | luxury-dark | organic>`, plus the chosen font pairing and 3 hex color tokens. Then build to that direction with full commitment.

Named-aesthetic definitions to embed so the weak model has concrete targets (from [NN/g on neobrutalism](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/neobrutalism/), [Bejamas](https://bejamas.com/blog/neubrutalism-web-design-trend), [Wuko Media](https://wukomedia.com/blog/brutalism-skeuomorphism-or-glassmorphism-web-design/)):

- **Linear/Vercel-style:** dark canvas (#08090a–#0d0e10), near-white text, one saturated accent, system-ish but tight type, hairline 1px borders, generous whitespace, subtle gradient glows.
- **Glassmorphism:** semi-transparent panels, `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)`, 1px translucent white border, layered over a colorful/blurred background for depth.
- **Neo-brutalism:** thick black borders, hard offset box-shadows (no blur), flat saturated colors, bold sans, compartmentalized boxes, intentional grid-breaking.
- **Editorial:** large serif display (Playfair/Fraunces), high size contrast, asymmetric columns, restrained palette.

---

## TIER 2 — Inject an explicit design system (tokens) so the model never invents arbitrary values

A weak model produces inconsistent spacing/sizing. Hard-code the scales as CSS variables in the prompt and instruct it to use *only* these tokens. This is exactly what v0 does internally ("spacing systems: rhythmic layout patterns," "typography scales: harmonious text hierarchy," consistent border radii — [v0 system prompt](https://agentic-design.ai/prompt-hub/vercel/v0-20250306)). 8px-base spacing and a modular type scale are the industry standard ([Designary](https://blog.designary.com/p/spacing-systems-and-scales-ui-design), [FontFYI type scale](https://fontfyi.com/blog/building-type-scale-design-system/)):

```css
:root{
  /* 8px spacing scale — use ONLY these */
  --s-1:4px; --s-2:8px; --s-3:12px; --s-4:16px; --s-6:24px;
  --s-8:32px; --s-12:48px; --s-16:64px; --s-24:96px; --s-32:128px;
  /* modular type scale (1.25 ratio) */
  --t-sm:.8rem; --t-base:1rem; --t-lg:1.25rem; --t-xl:1.563rem;
  --t-2xl:1.953rem; --t-3xl:2.441rem; --t-4xl:3.052rem; --t-5xl:3.815rem;
  /* tokens — fill per DIRECTION */
  --bg:#08090a; --surface:#111214; --text:#e6e6e6; --muted:#8a8f98;
  --accent:#5e6ad2; --border:rgba(255,255,255,.08); --radius:12px;
}
```

Typography rubric to enforce (Anthropic's isolated typography prompt — pastable):

> Never use: Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, system fonts. Pick from — code: JetBrains Mono / Fira Code; editorial: Playfair Display / Fraunces / Crimson Pro; startup: Clash Display / Satoshi / Cabinet Grotesque; technical: IBM Plex. Pairing principle: high contrast (display + mono, serif + geometric sans). Use weight extremes (100/200 vs 800/900, not 400 vs 600) and size jumps of 3x+, not 1.5x. Load from Google Fonts. State your choice before coding.

This converts vague taste into copy-pasteable rules a weak model can follow mechanically — the highest-leverage form of scaffolding.

---

## TIER 3 — Default animation toolkit, with canonical CDN snippets to embed

The cookbook's key insight for "wow per token": **one orchestrated staggered page-load reveal beats scattered micro-interactions.** Tell the model to default to that. Ranked by wow-per-token for a text-only model emitting a single HTML file:

**1. CSS-only staggered reveal (highest ROI — zero deps, always works).** Make this the *default*:
```css
@keyframes rise{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(20px)}to{opacity:1;transform:none}}
.reveal{animation:rise .6s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) both}
.reveal:nth-child(1){animation-delay:.05s} .reveal:nth-child(2){animation-delay:.12s}
.reveal:nth-child(3){animation-delay:.19s} /* ...stagger via animation-delay */
```

**2. CSS scroll-driven animations** (no JS, reveal-on-scroll). Modern, Chromium + Firefox-flagged ([Chrome for Developers](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/css-ui/scroll-driven-animations), [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_scroll-driven_animations)):
```css
.card{animation:rise linear both; animation-timeline:view(); animation-range:entry 0% cover 30%;}
```

**3. GSAP + ScrollTrigger** — best wow-per-token for JS scroll work; the model knows it well. CDN + idiomatic snippets (verified via Context7 GSAP docs + [GSAP ScrollTrigger docs](https://gsap.com/docs/v3/Plugins/ScrollTrigger/)):
```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.12.5/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.12.5/dist/ScrollTrigger.min.js"></script>
<script>
gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger);
// batch reveal-on-scroll with stagger (idiomatic):
ScrollTrigger.batch(".card",{onEnter:b=>gsap.to(b,{autoAlpha:1,y:0,stagger:.1})});
// pinned scrub section:
gsap.to(".panel",{xPercent:-100,ease:"none",
  scrollTrigger:{trigger:".wrap",pin:true,scrub:.5,end:"+=2000"}});
</script>
```

**4. Motion (motion.dev, the Motion One/Framer successor)** — clean ESM via CDN, great stagger ([motion.dev quick-start](https://motion.dev/docs/quick-start), [stagger](https://motion.dev/docs/stagger)):
```html
<script type="module">
import {animate,stagger,scroll} from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/motion@latest/+esm";
animate("li",{opacity:[0,1],y:[20,0]},{delay:stagger(0.08)});
</script>
```
For React, the cookbook explicitly says: "Use Motion library for React when available" (`framer-motion` / `motion`).

**5. anime.js v4** — ESM via CDN ([animejs docs](https://animejs.com/documentation/getting-started/imports-old/)):
```html
<script type="module">
import {animate,stagger} from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/animejs@4.0.0/+esm";
animate(".item",{translateY:[-20,0],opacity:[0,1],delay:stagger(100,{from:"center"}),duration:600});
</script>
```

**6. View Transitions API** — page/state transitions ([MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API/Using)): same-doc `document.startViewTransition(()=>{/*update DOM*/})`; cross-doc just needs `@view-transition{navigation:auto;}` in CSS of both pages.

**Default rule for the prompt:** "Default to CSS-only staggered page-load reveals. If JS is allowed and scroll choreography is wanted, load GSAP+ScrollTrigger from the exact CDN tags above. Never hand-roll easing — use cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) or GSAP power eases."

## TIER 4 — Generate → self-critique → refine loop (a harness multiplier, not a prompt line)

This is where a weak model gains the most at runtime. **Self-Refine** (Madaan et al., 2023) shows a *single* LLM acting as generator → feedback-provider → refiner, with no training, yields **~20% absolute average improvement** across 7 tasks including code optimization — and explicitly states "even GPT-4 can be further improved at test time" ([arXiv 2303.17651](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651)). The gain is *larger* for weaker models because they leave more on the table in one pass.

For frontend specifically, the design-critique research shows the feedback must be **grounded and rubric-scored**: UICrit feeds the model a screenshot, has it emit critiques tied to regions/bounding boxes plus a **1–5 design-quality rating**, and iterative refinement of the critique improves specificity ([UICrit, arXiv 2407.08850](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.08850); [Visual Prompting w/ Iterative Refinement, arXiv 2412.16829](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16829)).

Harness recipe (works text-only, since groq/compound has no vision — critique the *code*, not a screenshot):

1. **Generate** the HTML to the design system + DIRECTION.
2. **Critique** with a forced design-critic persona and a numeric rubric, e.g.:
   > You are a senior product designer. Score the code 1–5 on each: (a) typography contrast & non-default fonts, (b) color cohesion & accent discipline, (c) spacing rhythm (are all values on the 8px scale?), (d) animation orchestration (is there one staggered load reveal?), (e) atmosphere/background depth, (f) layout interest (asymmetry/grid-breaking vs 3-card-row). For every score <4, give one concrete, line-level fix. End with the lowest score.
3. **Refine** by feeding the critique back: "Apply every fix where score <4. Output the full revised file."
4. **Loop** until min score ≥4 or 2–3 iterations (Self-Refine shows diminishing returns after ~2–3).

The rubric is what makes a *weak* model's self-critique useful: it can't generate good feedback freely, but it can grade against an explicit checklist and act on the failures.

What the leaked scaffolds actually enforce — fold these constraints in:

- **bolt.new** (verbatim): *"For all designs I ask you to make, have them be beautiful, not cookie cutter. Make webpages that are fully featured and worthy for production."* Plus: JSX + Tailwind + React hooks + **Lucide React** for icons; *"Do not install other packages for UI themes, icons, etc unless absolutely necessary"*; use **Unsplash** stock photos by URL only (link, don't download). ([bolt prompt](https://huggingface.co/spaces/AntDX316/HF-Spaces/blob/main/.bolt/prompt), [x1xhlol leak repo](https://github.com/x1xhlol/system-prompts-and-models-of-ai-tools))
- **v0**: defaults to **shadcn/ui** + **Tailwind CSS variable–based color tokens**, **mobile-first responsive** required, **WCAG 2.1 compliance built-in** (semantic HTML + ARIA), **Framer Motion** for animation. ([v0 prompt](https://agentic-design.ai/prompt-hub/vercel/v0-20250306), [Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2024/Nov/25/leaked-system-prompts-from-vercel-v0/))
- **Common thread:** lean, opinionated stack + non-negotiable quality floors (responsive, accessible, production-worthy, no cookie-cutter). Lock the stack so the weak model never wanders.

Concrete constraints to add to the system prompt: *"Icons: Lucide only. Images: Unsplash URLs only. Must be mobile-first responsive and WCAG 2.1 (semantic HTML, ARIA labels, visible focus states). Use only the CSS variables defined above for color/spacing."*

## Suggested assembly order in the system prompt / skill file

1. The `<frontend_aesthetics>` slop-ban block (Tier 1).
2. Forced `DIRECTION:` manifesto line + named-aesthetic definitions (Tier 1).
3. Token CSS block + typography rubric (Tier 2).
4. Animation defaults + the exact CDN snippets (Tier 3).
5. Hard constraints: Lucide, Unsplash, responsive, WCAG, tokens-only (Tier 5).
6. In the harness loop, the rubric-scored critic persona + refine pass (Tier 4).

**Net:** Tiers 1–2 alone (banning defaults + injecting a token system + forcing a committed direction) capture most of the quality jump and cost only prompt tokens. Tier 4's critique loop is the runtime multiplier that disproportionately helps a weak model. Tier 3 supplies the "wow," and Tier 5 the production floor.
